newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-St George profit seen higher.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-St George profit seen higher.

text.p: Australian regional bank St George Bank Ltd is expected to report a modest rise in profits for the year to September 30 when it reports next Tuesday, reflecting the bank's expanding business banking operations.
BZW Investment Management Australia Ltd's BARCEP analysts' survey pegs St George's net profit after preference dividends at A$152 million, up 12 percent from a year earlier.
Forecasts ranged between A$139 million and A$165 million.

"St George is certainly being squeezed just as hard as other banks by the increased competition in the mortgage market but it should benefit from its expanding business banking business and from reduced costs," a Melbourne-based analyst said.
The bank had net earnings of A$135.5 million in the year to September 30, 1995 and predicted in May that 1995/96 earnings would be comfortably above the previous year.
In July, St George reaffirmed its expectations in a letter to shareholders in which it said it still expected to report higher annual earnings based on its operating performance.
One analyst said the market would be looking for any indication of the churn rate in St George's housing loan portfolio, particularly given the effect of the recent cuts in home loan rates.
"The faster the rate of churn then the faster their average margin on those loans is coming down," a senior Sydney-based banking analyst said.
On October 14, St George announced that it had agreed to a A$2.65 billion takeover of fellow Sydney-based regional bank, Advance Bank Ltd.

Last month ratings agency Standard & Poor's said it expected to assign a stable outlook to the merged bank but until the merger was finalised, St George would keep its current ratings of A/A-2 and remain under positive credit watch.

"The merger should provide St George with greater flexibility to withstand competitive pressures which continue to build in the Australian banking industry. The main benefits of the merger will be in market position and geographic diversity," S&P said.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has said it would not oppose the takeover and the two banks announced today they had completed a due diligence and neither party had decided to terminate the merger.

Analysts have said that while Advance shareholders were receiving top dollar for their investment, the move would help ensure St George's independence from takeover by larger major bank rivals such as National Australia Bank Ltd.

"The major point we should look for on St George is a warning that if they don't get Advance there'll be an affect on their profits because of an expected contraction in the housing loan market," the Sydney banking analyst said. At 3.50 p.m. (0450 GMT), St George shares were down nine cents at A$8.80.
